info.title: AutoX API
info.description:
Vehicle marketplace API. Headless and API-first: this document is the whole contract, and the Angular web app and a future native mobile app consume exactly these endpoints.

**Conventions that apply everywhere:**

* **Money** is an integer in the currency's minor unit, with an ISO 4217 code beside it. `priceAmount: 1850000, priceCurrencyCode: "EUR"` is €18,500.00. The scale comes from `GET /api/v1/reference/countries`.
* **Distance** is always kilometres on the wire, whatever a market displays.
* **Errors** are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Branch on `code`, never on `detail` — `detail` is English developer text and is not translated. Validation failures add a flat `errors` array of `{field, message}`.
* **Enums** serialise as their constant name. The full set a client may receive is at `GET /api/v1/reference/enums`; display labels are the client's own responsibility.
* **List endpoints are cursor-paginated.** Pass the previous response's `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. There are no page numbers and no total count.
* **Images are never uploaded through this API.** Request a slot, PUT the bytes straight to object storage with the pre-signed URL, then confirm.

put.description: Replaces the gallery order. The body must list every confirmed photo exactly once.

post.description:
Changes the password. Requires the current one, even though the request is already authenticated: a valid token may be a stolen one, and taking over the account permanently is the most valuable thing that can be done with it.

Returns a new token pair, and invalidates every existing session including the caller's. The client must store the tokens from this response; the refresh token it arrived with no longer works. An access token carries no reference to the session it was issued with, so "all sessions but this one" is not something the server can express — replacing the lot is the version of that guarantee it can actually keep.

get.description:
Search the live listings. Every filter is optional; no filters means everything visible.

Paginated by cursor, not by page number: nextCursor from one response is cursor in the next. There is no page number and no total, because offset paging over a table being written to skips and repeats rows, and a count costs a second scan.

post.summary:
Creates an account and signs it in, returning the same token pair as login — so a
 client never has to follow registration with a second call
post.description:
Creates an account and signs it in, returning the same token pair as login — so a client never has to follow registration with a second call.

role chooses PARTICULIER or PROFESSIONNEL; a professional must also send companyName and registrationNumber. ADMIN cannot be self-assigned.

post.summary: Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair.
post.description:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new pair. The old refresh token is invalid
 afterwards — clients must store the one returned here.

post.summary: Sets a new password using the token from a reset link
post.description:
Sets a new password using the token from a reset link.

The link works once and only for a short window. Every way it can fail — unknown, expired, already spent, replaced by a newer request — answers 400 INVALID_RESET_TOKEN, because a legitimate user does the same thing in all four cases: ask for a new link.

A successful reset ends every session on every device. The user signs in again.

post.summary:
Asks for a password reset link, which is emailed to the address if it belongs to an
 account that can use one
post.description:
Asks for a password reset link, which is emailed to the address if it belongs to an account that can use one.

Always 202, and always the same body, whether or not the address is registered: anything else would turn this into a way to find out who has an account here. The caller therefore cannot tell from the response that anything was sent. Repeated requests answer 429 RATE_LIMITED — the address does not have to be one the caller owns, so the endpoint is capped both per account and per caller.
Ends this device's session. Idempotent: an unknown token still returns 204.

post.summary: Exchanges credentials for a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token
post.description:
Exchanges credentials for a short-lived access token and a long-lived refresh token.

A wrong password and an unknown address both answer 401 INVALID_CREDENTIALS, deliberately indistinguishable. Repeated failures answer 429 TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS with Retry-After; the delay is progressive and capped, so failing on purpose cannot lock the real owner out.

patch.description:
Partial update: only the fields present in the body are changed. Email and role are
 not editable here — changing an address needs to prove control of the new one, and
 changing a role is a commercial decision, not a profile edit. The password has its
 own endpoint below.

One listing, as a buyer sees it: full description, equipment codes and the image gallery

get.description:
One listing, as a buyer sees it: full description, equipment codes and the image gallery in order, each image with its three size variants.

404 unless the listing is ACTIVE, not rejected, not soft-deleted and not past its expiry — including when the caller happens to be its owner, who reads it at /api/v1/listings/mine/{id} instead. The VIN, the seller's email and the exact coordinates are not part of this response.

status is not among them: state changes go through their own endpoints, which is what makes the transition rules unbypassable. Editing an ACTIVE listing is allowed and keeps it live.

get.summary:
The open markets: default locale, currency and the currency's minor-unit scale, which a
 client needs in order to render the integer prices this API returns.
get.description:
The open markets: default locale, currency and the currency's minor-unit scale, which a
 client needs in order to render the integer prices this API returns.

Every live session, newest first.

Not paginated, and the one list endpoint in the API that is not. The bound is how many devices one person signs in from, which is single digits: a page parameter here would be ceremony around a list that cannot grow.

The response cannot say which entry is the caller's own. An access token carries no reference to the refresh family it was issued with, so a client that wants to mark one as "this device" should match on the deviceLabel it chose at sign-in.

get.summary: The seller's own listings, in every state.
get.description: The seller's own listings, in every state. Paginated; there is no unbounded form.

get.summary: The seller's own view: full detail in any state, including drafts
get.description:
The seller's own view: full detail in any state, including drafts.

Under /mine/ rather than at /listings/{id} because that path is now the public detail endpoint, and one path returning two different shapes depending on who is asking makes for a contract no typed client can rely on.

get.summary: Accounts, newest first, optionally filtered by role
get.description:
Accounts, newest first, optionally filtered by role. Paginated by page number rather than by cursor: this is an operator tool over a slowly growing table, where jumping to a page is worth more than the consistency a cursor gives.

Closed accounts are excluded. Password hashes are never included.

delete.description:
Ends one session. The device holding it can no longer refresh, and its access token stops working when it expires — within fifteen minutes, which is the cost of a stateless API and the reason that lifetime is short.

A session belonging to someone else, or one already ended, answers 404: there is nothing to be learned here by guessing identifiers.

delete.summary: Removes the photo, its variants and the stored objects, and closes the ordering gap.
delete.description: Removes the photo, its variants and the stored objects, and closes the ordering gap.

ReorderImagesRequest.description:
The gallery's new order, front to back. Position 0 is the cover photo.

Must be a complete permutation of the listing's ready images — a partial list is rejected rather than interpreted, because "move this one to the front" and "these are the only ones I know about" are indistinguishable otherwise, and guessing wrong silently reorders someone's gallery.

ImageResponse.description:
One photo as the API exposes it: an id, its place in the gallery, and a URL per variant.

Storage keys are not exposed. A client that knew them could construct URLs we did not issue, and changing bucket layout would then be a breaking API change.

VariantView.description: Dimensions travel with the URL so a client can reserve layout space before loading.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: Password change for a signed-in account.

currentPassword.description:
proof that the caller is the owner and not the holder of a stolen
                        access token

newPassword.description: same single rule as registration: length, no composition theatre

deviceLabel.description:
label for the session this call establishes, since the change ends
                        every existing one. Omitted, the new session is simply unlabelled.

AuthResponse.description:
What login and refresh return.

expiresInSeconds is included alongside the absolute instant so a client with a skewed clock can still schedule its refresh correctly.

UserSummary.description: The compact user shape embedded in auth responses.

CreateListingRequest.description:
A new listing. Created as a DRAFT; nothing here publishes it.

Two either/or rules are enforced before the request reaches the service, mirroring the database's own constraints:

  • Vehicle: each of make and model is given either as a catalogue id or as text, never both and never neither. A trim requires a model.
  • Location: either a gazetteer place id, or postal code plus city as text while the gazetteer is unavailable.
Numeric bounds repeat the table's CHECK constraints so a bad value is a 400 with a field name rather than a 500 from the driver.

EmissionClass.description: Mirrors ck_listing_emission_class. Drives low-emission-zone filters in FR/DE.

ExteriorColor.description: Searchable colour family. Mirrors ck_listing_exterior_color. The manufacturer's own colour name goes in Listing.colorText.

ListingResponse.description:
The owner's view of a listing. Includes the states and timestamps a seller needs to understand what will happen next, and allowedTransitions so a client can render exactly the buttons that will work rather than guessing the state machine.

The public buyer-facing shape will be narrower — no VIN, no moderation detail — and arrives with search.

ListingStatus.description:
Seller-facing lifecycle, and the authority on which moves between states are legal. Mirrors ck_listing_status.

The transition table lives here rather than in the service so there is exactly one definition of what is allowed, and an illegal move is rejected rather than quietly applied. Transitions are about the shape of the lifecycle only — who may make a move, and whether a quota permits it, are separate questions answered by the service. 

   DRAFT ──publish──▶ ACTIVE ──unpublish──▶ PAUSED ──publish──▶ ACTIVE
                        │                     │
                        ├──▶ SOLD ◀───sold────┘
                        ├──▶ EXPIRED ──renew──▶ ACTIVE
                        └──▶ REMOVED  (terminal, see below)

LocationView.description: resolved is false while the location is still unmatched free text.

ModerationStatus.description: Admin verdict, independent of {@link ListingStatus ListingStatus}. Mirrors ck_listing_moderation_status.

VehicleView.description: fromCatalogue is false when the vehicle is identified by free text.

ImageUploadRequest.description:
Asks for a pre-signed upload URL.

The declared size is not a courtesy: it is signed into the URL, so storage rejects an upload of any other length. That is what stops a client from announcing a 2 MB photo and then pushing 2 GB through a URL we handed it.

ImageUploadTicket.description:
Everything a client needs to upload one photo, and nothing about our storage layout.

The client PUTs the bytes to uploadUrl with exactly requiredHeaders, then calls the confirm endpoint with imageId. The bytes never touch the API.

RegisterRequest.description:
Registration payload.

role accepts PARTICULIER or PROFESSIONNEL only — ADMIN is created out of band and can never be self-assigned through this endpoint.

RefreshRequest.description:
The refresh token travels in the body, not in a cookie: a native app has no
 cookie jar, and the same contract has to serve both clients.

token.description: the value from the emailed link's token parameter

ForgotPasswordRequest.description:
Asks for a reset link.

The address is validated for shape only. Whether it belongs to an account is not reported back, by design — see PasswordResetService.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
Partial profile update. A null member means "leave unchanged"; a blank string clears an optional field.

Email and password are deliberately absent. Changing an email has to re-trigger verification, and changing a password has to revoke every other session — both are their own endpoints, not a field in a profile PATCH.

UserProfileResponse.description:
The full own-profile view. The password hash and the internal version counter are
 not represented here at all, so they cannot leak by accident.

UpdateListingRequest.description:
Partial update. null means "leave unchanged".

Status is not a field here: moving between states goes through the publish, unpublish, renew and delete endpoints, which is what makes the transition rules impossible to bypass. Nor is the seller — a listing never changes hands.

Vehicle and location identification may be switched between catalogue reference and free text, but only coherently: supplying a makeId clears makeText and the reverse, and supplying both is rejected.

Model.description: yearFrom/yearTo bound the year filter; null means unknown or current.

Feature.description:
One item of equipment.

code is the identity and the only thing other endpoints exchange. labels is keyed by BCP 47 tag — fr-FR and en are seeded. A client that wants a locale with no row falls back to the language-only tag, then to en, then to the code; the endpoint returns what exists rather than guessing.

FeatureCategory.description: Mirrors ck_vehicle_feature_category. Groups equipment in the listing form and detail page.

Enums.description:
Every enum a client has to map, keyed by the name the API documents it under.

The values, not the labels. Display text belongs in the frontend's own translation files — there is no translation table for enums and inventing one would put French strings in a database that is never the right place to edit them. What the frontend cannot safely duplicate is the set of constants, and that is what this returns: a value appearing here that the frontend has no translation for is a visible gap, where a hardcoded list silently omits it.

Country.description:
An open market.

No localised country name: code is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 value, and a browser renders it in the user's own language with Intl.DisplayNames better than a seeded string could. name is the endonym, for logs and admin screens.

currencyMinorUnit is the one field a price-rendering client cannot do without: every amount in this API is an integer of the minor unit, and dividing by the wrong power of ten is off by a hundred.

SessionResponse.description:
One live session of the signed-in account.

id is the rotation family, not the token row. A session's token is replaced on every refresh, so the row id would change under the client between two reads of the list; the family is stable for the life of the session and is what the revoke endpoint takes.

Nothing here is a credential. The token itself is not in the database in a usable form at all, let alone in this response.

id.description: the session identifier, to pass to DELETE /me/sessions/{id}

deviceLabel.description: what the client called itself at sign-in; null if it said nothing

userAgent.description: raw User-Agent header, for a client that wants to name the device itself

ipAddress.description: where the session was created from, so an unexpected one is noticeable

lastUsedAt.description: when it last refreshed; null if it never has

expiresAt.description: when it dies on its own

ListingSearchCriteria.description:
Everything a buyer can filter on. Every field is optional; an empty criteria object means "all visible listings".

Make and model can each be given two ways, and both are needed:

  • makeId matches the catalogue exactly — precise, and what the frontend's dropdown will send once the catalogue exists.
  • make matches the displayed name, catalogue row or free text. Until the catalogue is seeded, every listing identifies its vehicle by text, so an id-only filter would match nothing at all.

SearchSort.description:
The orderings public search supports.

Each one is a keyset sort, so each needs a column that is non-null on every visible listing, plus id as a tie-breaker to make the order total. Without the tie-breaker two listings at the same price would have an undefined relative order, and a cursor sitting between them would either skip or repeat rows.

CursorPagePublicListingSummary.description:
A page of search results.

No total count, deliberately. Counting the matches for an arbitrary filter combination means a second full scan of the result set on every page, which costs more than the page itself and grows with the catalogue. Infinite scroll — which is what a phone does — needs nextCursor and nothing else.

When a result count does become a product requirement, the answer is a cached approximate count per filter combination, or Elasticsearch, not a COUNT(*) on the hot path.

PublicListingSummary.description:
One result card.

Every enumerated value is the stable code, never a display string: "DIESEL", not "Diesel" and certainly not "Gazole". The French frontend maps codes to French; nothing here assumes a language.

No seller contact details, no VIN, no moderation state. A search result is public, and a scraper gets exactly what a buyer's screen shows.

SellerCard.description: What a buyer sees about who is selling: a name and whether it is a trade seller.

PublicListingDetail.description:
The buyer-facing detail page.

Narrower than the seller's own view of the same listing. Absent on purpose: the VIN (identifies the vehicle and indirectly its owner), the moderation state (an internal matter), the exact coordinates, and anything about the seller beyond a display name.

As in the summary, every enumerated value is a stable code and every feature is a code. There is no human-readable label anywhere in this response.

SellerView.description: role tells a buyer whether this is a dealer or a private sale. Nothing more.

ListingSummary.description:
The row shape for a seller's listing list. Narrow on purpose: a dashboard with fifty
 rows should not carry fifty VINs and fifty descriptions over a mobile connection.

PageResponseListingSummary.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

PageResponseUserSummary.description:
The envelope every list endpoint returns.

Spring's own Page serialises its internal structure, which would tie the public contract to a Spring Data version. This is our shape, and it is the only one a mobile client has to understand.

Offset paging is correct for admin tables. Public search will use a keyset cursor instead — same envelope, with a nextCursor added — because offset paging skips and repeats rows while listings are being inserted underneath.

ApiError.description: RFC 9457 problem+json, extended with a stable `code`. Branch on `code`, never on `detail` — `detail` is untranslated developer text.

message.example: must be a well-formed email address

bearerAuth.description: Access token from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Short-lived (15 minutes); exchange the refresh token at `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` when it expires. Issuer: https://api.autox.local
